{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_017S3bVpVK99cbkG3bJmCqju","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# Systemedx Inc — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-15\n     4→Developer website: https://www.systemedx.com/\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→Systemedx Inc is a small, privately held healthcare technology company headquartered in Cullman, Alabama, founded in 1997. The company was originally chartered to provide document management systems to businesses and healthcare organizations, and later pivoted to focus on healthcare IT. The CEO is Kevin Bonner. The company has an estimated 11–50 employees and revenue in the $1–6 million range (sources vary). They also have an office in Alexandria, Louisiana.\n     9→\n    10→Systemedx is a small-scale EHR vendor serving ambulatory practices. They are not widely reviewed on third-party platforms — Slashdot/SourceForge lists the product but has zero user reviews. The company does not appear on major review sites like G2 or Capterra with any meaningful review volume. Their customer base appears to be regional, concentrated in the Southeast U.S., with a notable presence in orthopedic and sports medicine practices. A Birmingham Medical News article describes a deployment at \"a practice of 43 sports medicine and orthopedic physicians\" that was an early adopter of their Surgical Pathways module.\n    11→\n    12→## Product: Systemedx Clinical Navigator\n    13→\n    14→CHPL ID: 11536\n    15→Version: 2024.12\n    16→Certification Date: 2024-11-26\n    17→\n    18→### What It Is\n    19→\n    20→Systemedx Clinical Navigator is an all-in-one ambulatory EHR and practice management system. It is a single integrated platform that combines electronic health records, practice management (scheduling, billing, claims), a patient portal, and a surgical pathways module. The certified module encompasses the full product — there is no indication of separate products or a larger platform beyond what is certified.\n    21→\n    22→The product is certified for 37 ONC criteria spanning clinical documentation (a)(1)–(a)(14), transitions of care (b)(1)–(b)(3), clinical quality measures (c)(1)–(c)(3), privacy/security (d), patient portal/VDT (e)(1), public health reporting (f)(1),(f)(2),(f)(5),(f)(7), FHIR API (g)(10), and Direct messaging (h)(1). This is a broad certification footprint for a small vendor.\n    23→\n    24→### Users & Market\n    25→\n    26→Clinical Navigator targets ambulatory practices — primarily physician offices and multi-physician group practices. The SED intended user description is simply \"Clinical Users.\" Based on the surgical pathways module and the Birmingham Medical News case study, orthopedic and sports medicine practices are a key customer segment.\n    27→\n    28→No specific customer count is published on the website or easily found in third-party sources. The company is small enough (11–50 employees, $1–6M revenue) that the customer base is likely modest — probably dozens to low hundreds of practice sites rather than thousands.\n    29→\n    30→End users include physicians/providers, clinical staff, front desk/scheduling staff, billing/coding staff, and patients (via the portal).\n    31→\n    32→### Modules & Functionality\n    33→\n    34→Based on the vendor website's dedicated pages for each area:\n    35→\n    36→**EHR / Clinical Documentation (ehrsolutions.html)**\n    37→- \"AI Office Visit\" — uses AI to identify patterns in documentation and optimize frequently used items; claims to enable users to \"write entire visit\" with minimal clicks\n    38→- \"Touch Orders\" — single-click actions to send orders to imaging, write medications, and document in the chart simultaneously\n    39→- Medication management with one-click prescribing of physician favorites and refills\n    40→- Prescription Drug Monitoring Program (PDMP) integration\n    41→- Controlled substance prescribing (EPCS)\n    42→- Automatic drug interaction checking\n    43→- Patient tracking to monitor exam room status\n    44→- Doctor-specific dashboards with customizable graphs and drill-down to individual patient records\n    45→- Customizable workflows, forms, and document templates\n    46→\n    47→**Practice Management (pmsolutions.html)**\n    48→- Scheduling with patient check-in/check-out tracking and wait time monitoring\n    49→- Patient registration/demographics — patients can enter demographic information from home (pre-visit)\n    50→- AI-assisted coding — analyzes coding patterns and insurance reimbursement data to suggest optimal CPT/ICD codes\n    51→- Claims worksheet — consolidates worklist management, account inquiry, and claim refiling\n    52→- Automated clean claim submission and auto-posting of remittance information\n    53→- Batched statement generation for approval\n    54→- Automated eligibility verification (mentioned on homepage)\n    55→- Claim scrubbing (mentioned on homepage)\n    56→- Financial dashboards with clinic comparisons using red/yellow/green status indicators\n    57→\n    58→**Patient Portal (portal.html)**\n    59→- Patient self-registration with demographic, insurance, and clinical data entry\n    60→- Appointment requests\n    61→- Medication refill requests\n    62→- Secure messaging with clinical staff (re: lab results, plans of care)\n    63→- Online statement viewing and bill pay\n    64→- Access to clinical summaries (both overall healthcare information and service-specific summaries)\n    65→\n    66→**Surgical Pathways (surgicalpathways.html + Birmingham Medical News article)**\n    67→- Surgical case tracking from start to finish\n    68→- AI-driven billing that analyzes surgeries to detect missed billing opportunities\n    69→- \"Rogue surgery detection\" — identifies procedures performed but not billed (article claims up to $100K/year/surgeon in recovered revenue)\n    70→- Automated CPT code suggestion (~80% accuracy, learns from adjustments)\n    71→- ICD coding optimization and automatic insurance appeal filing\n    72→- Procedure-specific task list generation (cardiac clearance, equipment ordering, OR scheduling, etc.)\n    73→- Patient text reminders for appointments, pre-surgery instructions, location maps, and post-op follow-up surveys\n    74→- Real-time dashboards for surgical pathway performance, revenue recovery, and compliance monitoring\n    75→- Mobile integration — surgeons can photograph hospital forms and send encrypted patient data to office\n    76→\n    77→**MIPS/Quality Reporting (mipssolutions.html)**\n    78→- Measure calculation dashboard with color-coded performance metrics\n    79→- Quality measures export compatible with QPP submission\n    80→- Registry reporting: immunization, survey, syndromic surveillance\n    81→- 20+ clinical quality measures tested for certification\n    82→\n    83→**Interfaces & Integrations (interfaces.html)**\n    84→- HL7 2.x interfaces for clinical data exchange\n    85→- Lab interfaces: LabCorp, Quest Diagnostics, Huntsville Hospital Lab, Decatur Morgan Hospital Lab, Marshall Medical Centers Lab, Indiana HIE, Intermountain Laboratory, APEX, Compass Lab\n    86→- Physical therapy: WebPT, ATI Indiana\n    87→- DME: MotionMD, Motion Medical\n    88→- Transcription/Dictation: Command Health, Nuance\n    89→- Imaging: Aspyra, RadInfo, Medstrat, WW XRay\n    90→- Other: Clearwave Kiosk, Expeditor, Oberd, Open Edge Payments, Relatient, Surgimate, WhitePlume\n    91→\n    92→**FHIR API (API/AppRegistration.html)**\n    93→- OAuth 2.0-based API through \"Systemedx XNet\" portal\n    94→- Supports standalone patient/user apps, EHR launch apps, and bulk data apps\n    95→- Developer and user portals for app registration\n    96→- Certified for (g)(7)–(g)(10) FHIR API criteria\n    97→\n    98→### Data & Content\n    99→\n   100→Based on the features described above, Clinical Navigator stores and manages:\n   101→\n   102→- **Patient demographics and registration data** — explicitly described as entered by patients or front desk staff, including insurance information\n   103→- **Clinical encounter documentation** — visit notes, AI-assisted office visit documentation, customizable templates\n   104→- **Medications** — prescribing, refills, medication lists, drug interactions, PDMP data, controlled substance records\n   105→- **Orders** — imaging orders, medication orders, lab orders (implied by \"Touch Orders\" and lab interfaces)\n   106→- **Lab results** — received via HL7 interfaces from LabCorp, Quest, and hospital labs; communicated to patients via portal messaging\n   107→- **Problems/diagnoses** — mentioned in EHI export page (\"medications, problems, etc.\") and implied by clinical documentation\n   108→- **Billing and claims data** — CPT codes, ICD codes, insurance claims, remittances, statements, eligibility verification results, claim scrubbing results\n   109→- **Scheduling data** — appointments, check-in/check-out, wait times\n   110→- **Surgical case data** — surgical pathways with task lists, procedure tracking, billing recovery, pre/post-op communication\n   111→- **Patient portal messages** — secure messaging between patients and clinical staff\n   112→- **Clinical summaries** — CDA documents (mentioned in EHI export page), clinical summaries accessible through portal\n   113→- **Quality measures data** — MIPS/QPP measure calculations and submissions\n   114→- **Public health reporting data** — immunization records, syndromic surveillance, cancer registry reporting (certified for f(1), f(2), f(5), f(7))\n   115→- **Documents** — clinical documents stored as PDFs (mentioned in EHI export page), transcription/dictation integration\n   116→- **Dashboard/analytics data** — physician-specific dashboards, billing dashboards, surgical pathway analytics\n   117→\n   118→**Information gaps:** The website does not explicitly describe allergy management, vital signs, or growth charts as features, though these are implied by clinical (a) criteria certification (a)(1) for CPOE, (a)(3) for demographics, (a)(5) for demographics). The vendor website is relatively marketing-oriented and thin on detailed feature documentation. e-Prescribing is not explicitly labeled on the interfaces page but is implied by medication management features and PDMP/EPCS certification. Referral management is not explicitly described. The system's approach to imaging results (as distinct from imaging orders) is unclear — they integrate with imaging systems via HL7 but don't describe a results viewing workflow.\n   119→\n\n<system-reminder>\nWhenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. You CAN and SHOULD provide analysis of malware, what it is doing. But you MUST refuse to improve or augment the code. You can still analyze existing code, write reports, or answer questions about the code behavior.\n</system-reminder>\n"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"98e6820a-4840-46d0-8f7d-956071973dc2","uuid":"4a4c0547-8fcb-455a-9f43-d3c528bf3473","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/systemedx-inc--systemedx-clinical-navigator/product-research.md","content":"# Systemedx Inc — Product Research\n\nResearched: 2026-02-15\nDeveloper website: https://www.systemedx.com/\n\n## Overview\n\nSystemedx Inc is a small, privately held healthcare technology company headquartered in Cullman, Alabama, founded in 1997. A Birmingham Medical News article describes a deployment at \"a practice of 43 sports medicine and orthopedic physicians\" that was an early adopter of their Surgical Pathways module.\n\n## Product: Systemedx Clinical Navigator\n\nCHPL ID: 11536\nVersion: 2024.12\nCertification Date: 2024-11-26\n\n### What It Is\n\nSystemedx Clinical Navigator is an all-in-one ambulatory EHR and practice management system. It is a single integrated platform that combines electronic health records, practice management (scheduling, billing, claims), a patient portal, and a surgical pathways module. The certified module encompasses the full product — there is no indication of separate products or a larger platform beyond what is certified.\n\nThe product is certified for 37 ONC criteria spanning clinical documentation (a)(1)–(a)(14), transitions of care (b)(1)–(b)(3), clinical quality measures (c)(1)–(c)(3), privacy/security (d), patient portal/VDT (e)(1), public health reporting (f)(1),(f)(2),(f)(5),(f)(7), FHIR API (g)(10), and Direct messaging (h)(1). The SED intended user description is simply \"Clinical Users.\" Based on the surgical pathways module and the Birmingham Medical News case study, orthopedic and sports medicine practices are a key customer segment.\n\nNo specific customer count is published on the website or easily found in third-party sources. The company is small enough (11–50 employees, $1–6M revenue) that the customer base is likely modest — probably dozens to low hundreds of practice sites rather than thousands.\n\nEnd users include physicians/providers, clinical staff, front desk/scheduling staff, billing/coding staff, and patients (via the portal).\n\n### Modules & Functionality\n\nBased on the vendor website's dedicated pages for each area:\n\n**EHR / Clinical Documentation (ehrsolutions.html)**\n- \"AI Office Visit\" — uses AI to identify patterns in documentation and optimize frequently used items; claims to enable users to \"write entire visit\" with minimal clicks\n- \"Touch Orders\" — single-click actions to send orders to imaging, write medications, and document in the chart simultaneously\n- Medication management with one-click prescribing of physician favorites and refills\n- Prescription Drug Monitoring Program (PDMP) integration\n- Controlled substance prescribing (EPCS)\n- Automatic drug interaction indicators\n\n**Patient Portal (portal.html)**\n- Patient self-registration with demographic, insurance, and clinical data entry\n- Appointment requests\n- Medication refill requests\n- Secure messaging with clinical staff (re: lab results, plans of care)\n- Online statement viewing and bill pay\n- Access to clinical summaries (both overall healthcare information and service-specific summaries)\n\n**Surgical Pathways (surgicalpathways.html + Birmingham Medical News article)**\n- Surgical case tracking from start to finish\n- AI-driven billing that analyzes surgeries to detect missed billing opportunities\n- \"Rogue surgery detection\" — identifies procedures performed but not billed (article claims up to $100K/year/surgeon in recovered revenue)\n- Automated CPT code Payments, Relatient, Surgimate, WhitePlume\n\n**FHIR API (API/AppRegistration.html)**\n- OAuth 2.0-based API through \"Systemedx XNet\" portal\n- Supports standalone patient/user apps, EHR launch apps, and bulk data apps\n- Developer and user portals for app registration\n- Certified for (g)(7)–(g)(10) FHIR API criteria\n\n### Data & Content\n\nBased on the features described above, Clinical Navigator stores and manages:\n\n- **Patient demographics and registration data** — explicitly described as entered by patients or front desk staff, including insurance information\n- **Clinical           <p>\n   150→                        The data export module is accessed via a job stream called \"CDAEXPORT\" and will show on the right as \"Data Export\". \n   151→                        In the module there are 3 main options for export: All Patients, Select Patients, and Single Patient.\n   152→                    </p>\n   153→                    <p>\n   154→                        Selecting the \"All Patients\" tab prompts the user to select a directory for the exported files to be saved to, a date range for\n   155→                        the data to be exported for each patient, and checkboxes to include chart documents and a human readable copy of the CDA.\n   156→                    </p>\n   157→                    <p>\n   158→                        Selecting the \"Select Patients\" tab will allow the same options but allow to select a subset of patients either manually or by \n   159→                        appointment date range.\n   160→                    </p>\n   161→                    <p>\n   162→                        Selecting \"Single Patient\" will allow the same options as the \"Select Patients\" tab but only allow for a single patient export.\n   163→                    </p>\n   164→                    <p>\n   165→                        The exported data and data formats are listed below:\n   166→                        <ul>\n   167→                            <li>&nbsp;&nbsp;• Patient demographics and distinct chart data (medications, problems, etc.) are exported as CDA XML files</li>\n   168→                            <li>&nbsp;&nbsp;• CDA files are also exported as human-readable HTML files named \"CDA.html\"</li>\n   169→                            <li>&nbsp;&nbsp;• Patient chart documents are exported as PDF documents and stored in a main \"Documents\" folder with each document type separated into their own folder</li>\n   170→                            <li>\n   171→                                &nbsp;&nbsp;• CDA files and other documents and images are placed into folders named in the order listed below with data separated with and underscore (\"_\") character\n   172→ </div>\n                <p style=\"color: black; \">\n                    EHR data export documentation:\n                </p>\n                <br>\n                <div>\n                    <p>\n                        The data export module is accessed via a job stream called \"CDAEXPORT\" and will show on the right as \"Data Export\". \n                        In the module there are 3 main options for export: All Patients, Select Patients, and Single Patient.\n                    </p>\n                    <p>\n                        Selecting the \"All Patients\" tab prompts the user to select a directory for the exported files to be saved to, a date range for\n                        the data to be exported for each patient, and checkboxes to include chart documents and a human readable copy of the CDA.\n                    </p>\n                    <p>\n                        Selecting the \"Select Patients\" tab will allow the same options but allow to select a subset of patients either manually or by \n                        appointment date range.\n                    </p>\n                    <p>\n                        Selecting \"Single Patient\" will allow the same options as the \"Select Patients\" tab but only allow for a single patient export.\n                    </p>\n                    <p>\n                        The exported data and data formats are listed below:\n                        <ul>\n                            <li>&nbsp;&nbsp;• Patient demographics and distinct chart data (medications, problems, etc.) are exported as CDA XML files</li>\n                            <li>&nbsp;&nbsp;• CDA files are also exported as human-readable HTML files named \"CDA.html\"</li>\n                            <li>&nbsp;&nbsp;• Patient chart documents are exported as PDF documents and stored in a main \"Documents\" folder with each document type separated into their own folder</li>\n                            <li>\n                                &nbsp;&nbsp;• CDA files and other documents and images are placed into folders named in the order listed below with data separated with and underscore (\"_\") character\n                                <ul>\n                                    <li>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;- Last Name</li>\n                                    <li>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;- First Name</li>\n                                    <li>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;- DOB</li>\n                                    <li>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;- PatientID</li>\n                                </ul>\n                            </li>\n                        </ul>\n                    </p>\n                </div>\n            </div>\n        </div>\n    </div>\n\n\n    <!-- Footer -->\n    <footer class=\"footer\">\n src=\"//code.jquery.com/jquery-1.10.2.js\"></script>\n     7→    <script>$(function () { $(\"#header\").load(\"Header.html\"); });</script>\n     8→</head>\n     9→<body>\n    10→    <div id=\"header\">\n    11→\n    12→    </div>\n    13→    <script>w3.includeHTML();</script>\n    14→    <h2>Application Registration</h2>\n    15→    <p>\n    16→        Application developers must register with Systemedx to obtain OAuth 2.0 client credentials used to communicate with our API endpoints (refer to our <a href=\"AuthorizationTechnical.html\" target=\"_blank\">authorization page</a> for details).\n    17→        Systemedx XNet API <a href=\"https://webservices2.systemedx.com/xnet/auth\" target=\"_blank\">portal</a> has 2 options for user logins.\n    18→        <ul>\n    19→            <li>\n    20→                The Developer Portal enables Systemedx FHIR API use by external developers.\n    21→            </li>\n    22→            <li>\n    23→                The User Portal is for Systemedx users and their patients.\n    24→            </li>\n    25→\n    26→        </ul>\n    27→        New users to the portal will have to register a new user account to login.\n    28→    </p>\n    29→\n    30→    <h3>Developer Portal</h3>\n    31→    <p>\n    32→        Once logged in to the developer dashboard, Developers can view or manage existing applications shown on the dashboard or can register new applications by clicking the \"Add Application\" Option.<br /><br />\n    33→        Developers will then choose the appropriate application type and fill out the required fields for that type.<br /><br />\n    34→        The following required fields are common to most app-types:\n    35→        <ul>\n    36→            <li>Client Name</li>\n    37→            <li>Client id (the id to be used to reference/authorize the application accross the api)</li>\n    38→            <li>Client Uri (launch URI)</li>\n    39→            <li>Redirect Uri</li>\n    40→            <li>Client Scopes authorized</li>\n    41→        </ul>\n    42→\n    43→\n    44→    </p>\n    45→    <p>\n    46→        After registration, the app will be placed in a waiting status while personel at Systemedx review the app registration.  <br />\n    47→        If more information/clarification about a certain aspect or use-case of the application is required, the developer may be contacted to make sure that the product registered is the appropriate fit for the use case. <br />\n    48→        Once approved, the application will be put into a Production status.\n    49→    </p>\n    50→\n    51→    <h3>User Portal</h3>\n    52→    <p>\n    53→        The user portal is where user's and patients of clinics utilizing Systemedx Clinical Navigator go and manage their access to API's that they have access to.  They will be able to link their individual identities from the clinic that they are associated with to the api and grant access within this portal.  The user will be provided a unique code from the clinic to be able to do this.\n    54→    </p>\n    55→    <h2>Information on App Types</h2>\n    56→    <ul>\n    57→        <li>\n    58→            <p>Standalone Patient App [Public or Confidential]:&nbsp &nbsp A 3-Legged OAuth app that launches from outside an EHR session, typically designed for direct patient interaction.</p>\n    59→        </li>\n    60→        <li>\n    61→            <p>Standalone User App [Public or Confidential]: &nbsp &nbsp   A 3-Legged OAuth app that launches from outside an EHR session, typically designed for interaction by medical personel or other healthcare entities.</p>\n    62→        </li>\n    63→        <li>\n    64→            <p>EHR Launch App [Public or Confidential]:  &nbsp &nbsp A 3-Legged OAuth app that launches from another EHR session/portal, typically designed for interaction by healthcare entities.</p>\n    65→        </li>\n    66→        <li>\n    67→            <p>Bulk Data App [Public]: &nbsp &nbsp A 2-Legged OAuth app that has no end user interface to be used to transmit/recieve bulk data between Systemedx XNet and another healthcare entity.</p>\n    68→        </li>\n    69→        <p>\n    70→            A note on <a href=\"https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6749#section-2.1\" target=\"_blank\">Public/Confidential</a> apps: &nbsp &nbsp The differentiation is based upon whether the execution environment within which the app runs enables the app to maintain the confidentiality of their client credentials.\n    71→        </p>\n    72→    </ul>\n    73→\n    74→</body>\n    75→</html>\n\n<system-reminder>\nWhenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. html>\n<html>\n<head>\n    <link href=\"default.css\" rel=\"Stylesheet\" type=\"text/css\">\n    <script src=\"https://www.w3schools.com/lib/w3.js\"></script>\n    <script src=\"//code.jquery.com/jquery-1.10.2.js\"></script>\n    <script>$(function () { $(\"#header\").load(\"Header.html\"); });</script>\n</head>\n<body>\n    <div id=\"header\">\n\n    </div>\n    <script>w3.includeHTML();</script>\n    <h2>Application Registration</h2>\n    <p>\n        Application developers must register with Systemedx to obtain OAuth 2.0 client credentials used to communicate with our API endpoints (refer to our <a href=\"AuthorizationTechnical.html\" target=\"_blank\">authorization page</a> for details).\n        Systemedx XNet API <a href=\"https://webservices2.systemedx.com/xnet/auth\" target=\"_blank\">portal</a> has 2 options for user logins.\n        <ul>\n            <li>\n                The Developer Portal enables Systemedx FHIR API use by external developers.\n            </li>\n            <li>\n                The User Portal is for Systemedx users and their patients.\n            </li>\n\n        </ul>\n        New users to the portal will have to register a new user account to login.\n    </p>\n\n    <h3>Developer Portal</h3>\n    <p>\n        Once logged in to the developer dashboard, Developers can view or manage existing applications shown on the dashboard or can register new applications by clicking the \"Add Application\" Option.<br /><br />\n        Developers will then choose the appropriate application type and fill out the required fields for that type.<br /><br />\n        The following required fields are common to most app-types:\n        <ul>\n            <li>Client Name</li>\n            <li>Client id (the id to be used to reference/authorize the application accross the api)</li>\n            <li>Client Uri (launch URI)</li>\n            <li>Redirect Uri</li>\n            <li>Client Scopes authorized</li>\n        </ul>\n\n\n    </p>\n    <p>\n        After registration, the app will be placed in a waiting status while personel at Systemedx review the app registration.  <br />\n        If more information/clarification about a certain aspect or use-case of the application is required, the developer may be contacted to make sure that the product registered is the appropriate fit for the use case. <br />\n        Once approved, the application will be put into a Production status.\n    </p>\n\n    <h3>User Portal</h3>\n    <p>\n        The user portal is where user's and patients of clinics utilizing Systemedx Clinical Navigator go and manage their access to API's that they have access to.  They will be able to link their individual identities from the clinic that they are associated with to the api and grant access within this portal.  The user will be provided a unique code from the clinic to be able to do this.\n    </p>\n    <h2>Information on App Types</h2>\n    <ul>\n        <li>\n            <p>Standalone Patient App [Public or Confidential]:&nbsp &nbsp A 3-Legged OAuth app that launches from outside an EHR session, typically designed for direct patient interaction.</p>\n        </li>\n        <li>\n            <p>Standalone User App [Public or Confidential]: &nbsp &nbsp   A 3-Legged OAuth app that launches from outside an EHR session, typically designed for interaction by medical personel or other healthcare entities.</p>\n        </li>\n        <li>\n            <p>EHR Launch App [Public or Confidential]:  &nbsp &nbsp A 3-Legged OAuth app that launches from another EHR session/portal, typically designed for interaction by healthcare entities.</p>\n        </li>\n        <li>\n            <p>Bulk Data App [Public]: &nbsp &nbsp A 2-Legged OAuth app that has no end user interface to be used to transmit/recieve bulk data between Systemedx XNet and another healthcare entity.</p>\n        </li>\n        <p>\n            A note on <a href=\"https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6749#section-2.1\" target=\"_blank\">Public/Confidential</a> apps: &nbsp &nbsp The differentiation is based upon whether the execution environment within which the app runs enables the app to maintain the confidentiality of their client credentials.\n        </p>\n    </ul>\n\n</body>\n</html>","numLines":75,"startLine":1,"totalLines":75}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Jp8FQ4ZhZ6eP2LvFE8GiJb","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→﻿<!DOCTYPE html>\n     2→<html>\n     3→<head>\n     4→    <link href=\"default.css\" rel=\"Stylesheet\" type=\"text/css\">\n     5→    <script src=\"https://www.w3schools.com/lib/w3.js\"></script>\n     6→    <script src=\"//code.jquery.com/jquery-1.10.2.js\"></script>\n     7→    <script>$(function () { $(\"#header\").load(\"Header.html\"); });</script>\n     8→</head>\n     9→<body>\n    10→    <div id=\"header\">\n    11→\n    12→    </div>\n    13→    <script>w3.includeHTML();</script>\n    14→    <h2>Authorization</h2>\n    15→    <p>\n    16→        Systemedx XNet API is secured by XNet Auth, an OAUTH 2.0 authorization server. <br />App developers that register with XNET are issued OAuth client credentials used to request access tokens (a type of JSON web token, JWT) from our authorization server.<br />\n    17→        An access token represents an app’s authorized access to one or more API endpoints used to read, write, or update data in the API, where an app is required to provide an\n    18→        access token to make a successful request to those endpoints.\n    19→    </p>\n    20→        <p>\n    21→            The following authorization methods are supported in XNet API:\n    22→            <ul>\n    23→                <li>\n    24→                    2-legged OAuth, in which apps use their OAuth client credentials to obtain an access token. This method is used where XNet users have authorized an app to access a specific set of endpoints for their organization. Our implementation of 2-legged OAuth uses the client credentials grant type as defined by OAuth 2.0.\n    25→                </li>\n    26→                <li>\n    27→                    3-legged OAuth, in which apps must get end user authorization to obtain an access token, in addition to providing their client credentials. This method is used for patient- and provider-facing apps accessing data on behalf of an end user. Our implementation of 3-legged OAuth uses the authorization code grant type as defined by OAuth 2.0.\n    28→                </li>\n    29→\n    30→            </ul>\n    31→        </p>\n    32→    <h2>Supported Scopes</h2>\n    33→    <p>\n    34→        Below are the supported scopes (or permissions) by our API. Access for the individual scopes can be requested/granted during user registration. Scopes indicated below are represented by \"r\" for Read and \"s\" for Search functionality.\n    35→        Items with \"rs\" have both scopes supported but a patient/user may have access granted to only one or the other.\n    36→    </p>\n    37→    <h3>Patient-Specific Scopes</h3>\n    38→    <p>\n    39→        Patient-specific scopes allow access to specific data about a single patient. Which patient is not specified here: clinical data scopes are all about what and not who which is handled in the next section. Patient-specific scopes start with patient/. Note that some EHRs may not enable access to all related resources (for example, Practitioners linked to/from Patient-specific resources). Note that if a FHIR server supports linking one Patient record with another via Patient.link, the server documentation SHALL describe its authorization behavior.\n    40→    </p>\n    41→    <ul>\n    42→        <li>patient/AllergyIntolerance.rs</li>\n    43→        <li>patient/CarePlan.rs</li>\n    44→        <li>patient/CareTeam.rs</li>\n    45→        <li>patient/Condition.rs</li>\n    46→        <li>patient/Device.rs</li>\n    47→        <li>patient/DiagnosticReport.rs</li>\n    48→        <li>patient/DocumentReference.rs</li>\n    49→        <li>patient/Encounter.rs</li>\n    50→        <li>patient/Goal.rs</li>\n    51→        <li>patient/Immunization.rs</li>\n    52→        <li>patient/Location.rs</li>\n    53→        <li>patient/Medication.rs</li>\n    54→        <li>patient/MedicationRequest.rs</li>\n    55→        <li>patient/Observation.rs</li>\n    56→        <li>patient/Organization.rs</li>\n    57→        <li>patient/Patient.rs</li>\n    58→        <li>patient/Practitioner.rs</li>\n    59→        <li>patient/PractitionerRole.rs</li>\n    60→        <li>patient/Procedure.rs</li>\n    61→        <li>patient/Provenance.r</li>\n    62→        <li>patient/Binary.r</li>\n    63→        <li>patient/*.rs</li>\n    64→    </ul>\n    65→    <h3>User-Level Scopes</h3>\n    66→    <p>\n    67→        User-level scopes allow access to specific data that a user can access. Note that this isn’t just data about the user; it’s data available to that user. User-level scopes start with user/.\n    68→    </p>\n    69→    <ul>\n    70→        <li>user/AllergyIntolerance.rs</li>\n    71→        <li>user/CarePlan.rs</li>\n    72→        <li>user/CareTeam.rs</li>\n    73→        <li>user/Condition.rs</li>\n    74→        <li>user/Device.rs</li>\n    75→        <li>user/DiagnosticReport.rs</li>\n    76→        <li>user/DocumentReference.rs</li>\n    77→        <li>user/Encounter.rs</li>\n    78→        <li>user/Goal.rs</li>\n    79→        <li>user/Immunization.rs</li>\n    80→        <li>user/Location.rs</li>\n    81→        <li>user/Medication.rs</li>\n    82→        <li>user/MedicationRequest.rs</li>\n    83→        <li>user/Observation.rs</li>\n    84→        <li>user/Organization.rs</li>\n    85→        <li>user/Patient.rs</li>\n    86→        <li>user/Practitioner.rs</li>\n    87→        <li>user/PractitionerRole.rs</li>\n    88→        <li>user/Procedure.rs</li>\n    89→        <li>user/Provenance.r</li>\n    90→        <li>user/Binary.r</li>\n    91→        <li>user/*.rs</li>\n    92→    </ul>\n    93→    <h3>System-Level Scopes</h3>\n    94→    <p>\n    95→        System-level scopes describe data that a client system is directly authorized to access; these scopes are useful in cases where there is no user in the loop, such as a data monitoring or reporting service. System-level scopes start with system/.\n    96→    </p>\n    97→    <ul>\n    98→        <li>system/AllergyIntolerance.r</li>\n    99→        <li>system/CarePlan.r</li>\n   100→        <li>system/CareTeam.r</li>\n   101→        <li>system/Condition.r</li>\n   102→        <li>system/Device.r</li>\n   103→        <li>system/DiagnosticReport.r</li>\n   104→        <li>system/DocumentReference.r</li>\n   105→        <li>system/Encounter.r</li>\n   106→        <li>system/Goal.r</li>\n   107→        <li>system/Immunization.r</li>\n   108→        <li>system/Location.r</li>\n   109→        <li>system/Medication.r</li>\n   110→        <li>system/MedicationRequest.r</li>\n   111→        <li>system/Observation.r</li>\n   112→        <li>system/Organization.r</li>\n   113→        <li>system/Patient.r</li>\n   114→        <li>system/Practitioner.r</li>\n   115→        <li>system/PractitionerRole.r</li>\n   116→        <li>system/Procedure.r</li>\n   117→        <li>system/Provenance.r</li>\n   118→        <li>system/Binary.r</li>\n   119→        <li>system/*.r</li>\n   120→        <li>system/*.d - for Delete rights</li>\n   121→    </ul>\n   122→\n   123→    <h2>Token Request</h2>\n   124→    <div style=\"line-height:10px\">\n   125→        <h3>Input Parameters</h3>\n   126→        <p>The app issues an HTTP POST to the EHR authorization server’s token endpoint URL.  For more info, visit the following <a href=\"http://hl7.org/fhir/smart-app-launch/STU2/app-launch.html#obtain-authorization-code\" target=\"_blank\">site</a>.</p>\n   127→        <h4>* = required</h4>\n   128→    </div>\n   129→    <table>\n   130→        <thead>\n   131→            <tr>\n   132→                <td>Parameter</td>\n   133→                <td>Type</td>\n   134→                <td>Value</td>\n   135→            </tr>\n   136→        </thead>\n   137→        <tbody>\n   138→            <tr>\n   139→                <td>grant_type*</td>\n   140→                <td>string</td>\n   141→                <td>\n   142→                    For 2-legged OAuth, the value is always client_credentials.<br />\n   143→                    For 3-legged OAuth, the value will be either authorization_code to initially request an access token, or refresh_token to obtain a new access token from a refresh token.\n   144→                </td>\n   145→\n   146→            </tr>\n   147→            <tr>\n   148→                <td>redirect_uri</td>\n   149→                <td>string</td>\n   150→                <td>The same redirect_uri used in the initial authorization request.(Required if grant_type is authorization_code)</td>\n   151→            </tr>\n   152→            <tr>\n   153→                <td>code</td>\n   154→                <td>string</td>\n   155→                <td>Code that the app received from the authorization server. (Required if grant_type is authorization code)</td>\n   156→            </tr>\n   157→            <tr>\n   158→                <td>code_verifier</td>\n   159→                <td>string</td>\n   160→                <td>This parameter is used to verify against the code_challenge parameter previously provided in the authorize request. (Required for token authentication using PKCE if grant_type is authorization_code)</td>\n   161→            </tr>\n   162→            <tr>\n   163→                <td>refresh_token</td>\n   164→                <td>string</td>\n   165→                <td>Required if grant_type is refresh_token. The value is the refresh token returned by the authorize endpoint.</td>\n   166→            </tr>\n   167→            <tr>\n   168→                <td>scope</td>\n   169→                <td>string</td>\n   170→                <td>This is required if the grant_type is client_credentials or refresh_token. The value is a space-delimited, case-sensitive string of the requested scopes. If the grant_type is a refresh_token, then the requested scopes must be a subset of those provided when the refresh token was originally created.</td>\n   171→            </tr>\n   172→            <tr>\n   173→                <td>client_id</td>\n   174→                <td>string</td>\n   175→                <td>Required for public apps. Omit for confidential apps. </td>\n   176→            </tr>\n   177→        </tbody>\n   178→    </table>\n   179→    <h3>Output Results</h3>\n   180→    <table>\n   181→        <thead>\n   182→            <tr>\n   183→                <td>Parameter</td>\n   184→                <td>Description</td>\n   185→            </tr>\n   186→        </thead>\n   187→        <tbody>\n   188→            <tr>\n   189→                <td>access_token</td>\n   190→                <td>The access token (JWT) issued by the authorization server</td>\n   191→            </tr>\n   192→            <tr>\n   193→                <td>token_type</td>\n   194→                <td>describes the access token; value is always “Bearer”</td>\n   195→            </tr>\n   196→            <tr>\n   197→                <td>expires_in</td>\n   198→                <td>Lifetime in seconds of the access token, after which the token SHALL NOT be accepted by the resource server</td>\n   199→            </tr>\n   200→            <tr>\n   201→                <td>scope</td>\n   202→                <td>Scope of access authorized. Note that this can be different from the scopes requested by the app.</td>\n   203→            </tr>\n   204→            <tr>\n   205→                <td>id_token</td>\n   206→                <td>Authenticated user identity and user details, if requested</td>\n   207→            </tr>\n   208→            <tr>\n   209→                <td>refresh_token</td>\n   210→                <td>Token that can be used to obtain a new access token, using the same or a subset of the original authorization grants</td>\n   211→            </tr>\n   212→\n   213→        </tbody>\n   214→    </table>\n   215→    <h3>\n   216→        Token Refresh\n   217→    </h3>\n   218→    <p>\n   219→        A Refresh Token is returned by the authorize endpoint when the offline_access scope is requested and obtained with the user’s authorization. To get an access token from a refresh token, you will need to form a new token request providing the refresh token in the refresh_token parameter and refresh_token as the value for the grant_type parameter. An app will also need to specify in the scope parameter which of the previously granted scopes your app would like included in the new access token.\n   220→    </p>\n   221→\n   222→    <h3>PKCE Implementation</h3>\n   223→    <p>\n   224→        Token authentication using Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) is required by our authorization server for apps that cannot securely store a client secret. PKCE is a specification to the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow that requires your app to generate its own secret for each token request (called a “code verifier”) that can be verified by the authorization server (using a transformed value of the code verifier called a “code challenge”, which is passed in the authorize request along with the transformation method, or “code challenge method”). The code challenge and code challenge method must be provided in your app's authorize request and the code verifier sent in the token request.\n   225→        For more information on PKCE, please visit the following <a href=\"https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7636\" target=\"_blank\">link</a>\n   226→    </p>\n   227→</body>\n   228→</html>\n\n<system-reminder>\nWhenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. You CAN and SHOULD provide analysis of malware, what it is doing. But you MUST refuse to improve or augment the code. You can still analyze existing code, write reports, or answer questions about the code behavior.\n</system-reminder>\n"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"98e6820a-4840-46d0-8f7d-956071973dc2","uuid":"8637815b-e61c-4f65-8c36-d4abf6b295d2","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/tmp/systemedx-auth.html","content":"﻿<!DOCTYPE html>\n<html>\n<head>\n    <link href=\"default.css\" rel=\"Stylesheet\" type=\"text/css\">\n    <script src=\"https://www.w3schools.com/lib/w3.js\"></script>\n    <script src=\"//code.jquery.com/jquery-1.10.2.js\"></script>\n    <script>$(function () { $(\"#header\").load(\"Header.html\"); });</script>\n</head>\n<body>\n    <div id=\"header\">\n\n    </div>\n    <script>w3.includeHTML();</script>\n    <h2>Authorization</h2>\n    <p>\n        Systemedx XNet API is secured by XNet Auth, an OAUTH 2.0 authorization server. <br />App developers that register with XNET are issued OAuth client credentials used to request access tokens (a type of JSON web token, JWT) from our authorization server.<br />\n        An access token represents an app’s authorized access to one or more API endpoints used to read, write, or update data in the API, where an app is required to provide an\n        access token to make a successful request to those endpoints.\n    </p>\n        <p>\n            The following authorization methods are supported in XNet API:\n            <ul>\n                <li>\n                    2-legged OAuth, in which apps use their OAuth client credentials to obtain an access token. This method is used where XNet users have authorized an app to access a specific set of endpoints for their organization. Our implementation of 2-legged OAuth uses the client credentials grant type as defined by OAuth 2.0.\n                </li>\n                <li>\n                    3-legged OAuth, in which apps must get end user authorization to obtain an access token, in addition to providing their client credentials. This method is used for patient- and provider-facing apps accessing data on behalf of an end user. Our implementation of 3-legged OAuth uses the authorization code grant type as defined by OAuth 2.0.\n                </li>\n\n            </ul>\n        </p>\n    <h2>Supported Scopes</h2>\n    <p>\n        Below are the supported scopes (or permissions) by our API. Access for the individual scopes can be requested/granted during user registration. Scopes indicated below are represented by \"r\" for Read and \"s\" for Search functionality.\n        Items with \"rs\" have both scopes supported but a patient/user may have access granted to only one or the other.\n    </p>\n    <h3>Patient-Specific Scopes</h3>\n    <p>\n        Patient-specific scopes allow access to specific data about a single patient. Which patient is not specified here: clinical data scopes are all about what and not who which is handled in the next section. Patient-specific scopes start with patient/. Note that some EHRs may not enable access to all related resources (for example, Practitioners linked to/from Patient-specific resources). Note that if a FHIR server supports linking one Patient record with another via Patient.link, the server documentation SHALL describe its authorization behavior.\n    </p>\n    <ul>\n        <li>patient/AllergyIntolerance.rs</li>\n        <li>patient/CarePlan.rs</li>\n        <li>patient/CareTeam.rs</li>\n        <li>patient/Condition.rs</li>\n        <li>patient/Device.rs</li>\n        <li>patient/DiagnosticReport.rs</li>\n        <li>patient/DocumentReference.rs</li>\n        <li>patient/Encounter.rs</li>\n        <li>patient/Goal.rs</li>\n        <li>patient/Immunization.rs</li>\n        <li>patient/Location.rs</li>\n        <li>patient/Medication.rs</li>\n        <li>patient/MedicationRequest.rs</li>\n        <li>patient/Observation.rs</li>\n        <li>patient/Organization.rs</li>\n        <li>patient/Patient.rs</li>\n        <li>patient/Practitioner.rs</li>\n        <li>patient/PractitionerRole.rs</li>\n        <li>patient/Procedure.rs</li>\n        <li>patient/Provenance.r</li>\n        <li>patient/Binary.r</li>\n        <li>patient/*.rs</li>\n    </ul>\n    <h3>User-Level Scopes</h3>\n    <p>\n        User-level scopes allow access to specific data that a user can access. Note that this isn’t just data about the user; it’s data available to that user. User-level scopes start with user/.\n    </p>\n    <ul>\n        <li>user/AllergyIntolerance.rs</li>\n        <li>user/CarePlan.rs</li>\n        <li>user/CareTeam.rs</li>\n        <li>user/Condition.rs</li>\n        <li>user/Device.rs</li>\n        <li>user/DiagnosticReport.rs</li>\n        <li>user/DocumentReference.rs</li>\n        <li>user/Encounter.rs</li>\n        <li>user/Goal.rs</li>\n        <li>user/Immunization.rs</li>\n        <li>user/Location.rs</li>\n        <li>user/Medication.rs</li>\n        <li>user/MedicationRequest.rs</li>\n        <li>user/Observation.rs</li>\n        <li>user/Organization.rs</li>\n        <li>user/Patient.rs</li>\n        <li>user/Practitioner.rs</li>\n        <li>user/PractitionerRole.rs</li>\n        <li>user/Procedure.rs</li>\n        <li>user/Provenance.r</li>\n        <li>user/Binary.r</li>\n        <li>user/*.rs</li>\n    </ul>\n    <h3>System-Level Scopes</h3>\n    <p>\n        System-level scopes describe data that a client system is directly authorized to access; these scopes are useful in cases where there is no user in the loop, such as a data monitoring or reporting service. System-level scopes start with system/.\n    </p>\n    <ul>\n        <li>system/AllergyIntolerance.r</li>\n        <li>system/CarePlan.r</li>\n        <li>system/CareTeam.r</li>\n        <li>system/Condition.r</li>\n        <li>system/Device.r</li>\n        <li>system/DiagnosticReport.r</li>\n        <li>system/DocumentReference.r</li>\n        <li>system/Encounter.r</li>\n        <li>system/Goal.r</li>\n        <li>system/Immunization.r</li>\n        <li>system/Location.r</li>\n        <li>system/Medication.r</li>\n        <li>system/MedicationRequest.r</li>\n        <li>system/Observation.r</li>\n        <li>system/Organization.r</li>\n        <li>system/Patient.r</li>\n        <li>system/Practitioner.r</li>\n        <li>system/PractitionerRole.r</li>\n        <li>system/Procedure.r</li>\n        <li>system/Provenance.r</li>\n        <li>system/Binary.r</li>\n        <li>system/*.r</li>\n        <li>system/*.d - for Delete rights</li>\n    </ul>\n\n    <h2>Token Request</h2>\n    <div style=\"line-height:10px\">\n        <h3>Input Parameters</h3>\n        <p>The app issues an HTTP POST to the EHR authorization server’s token endpoint URL.  For more info, visit the following <a href=\"http://hl7.org/fhir/smart-app-launch/STU2/app-launch.html#obtain-authorization-code\" target=\"_blank\">site</a>.</p>\n        <h4>* = required</h4>\n    </div>\n    <table>\n        <thead>\n            <tr>\n                <td>Parameter</td>\n                <td>Type</td>\n                <td>Value</td>\n            </tr>\n        </thead>\n        <tbody>\n            <tr>\n                <td>grant_type*</td>\n                <td>string</td>\n                <td>\n                    For 2-legged OAuth, the value is always client_credentials.<br />\n                    For 3-legged OAuth, the value will be either authorization_code to initially request an access token, or refresh_token to obtain a new access token from a refresh token.\n                </td>\n\n            </tr>\n            <tr>\n                <td>redirect_uri</td>\n                <td>string</td>\n                <td>The same redirect_uri used in the initial authorization request.(Required if grant_type is authorization_code)</td>\n            </tr>\n            <tr>\n                <td>code</td>\n                <td>string</td>\n                <td>Code that the app received from the authorization server. (Required if grant_type is authorization code)</td>\n            </tr>\n            <tr>\n                <td>code_verifier</td>\n                <td>string</td>\n                <td>This parameter is used to verify against the code_challenge parameter previously provided in the authorize request. (Required for token authentication using PKCE if grant_type is authorization_code)</td>\n            </tr>\n            <tr>\n                <td>refresh_token</td>\n                <td>string</td>\n                <td>Required if grant_type is refresh_token. The value is the refresh token returned by the authorize endpoint.</td>\n            </tr>\n            <tr>\n                <td>scope</td>\n                <td>string</td>\n                <td>This is required if the grant_type is client_credentials or refresh_token. The value is a space-delimited, case-sensitive string of the requested scopes. If the grant_type is a refresh_token, then the requested scopes must be a subset of those provided when the refresh token was originally created.</td>\n            </tr>\n            <tr>\n                <td>client_id</td>\n                <td>string</td>\n                <td>Required for public apps. Omit for confidential apps. </td>\n            </tr>\n        </tbody>\n    </table>\n    <h3>Output Results</h3>\n    <table>\n        <thead>\n            <tr>\n                <td>Parameter</td>\n                <td>Description</td>\n            </tr>\n        </thead>\n        <tbody>\n            <tr>\n                <td>access_token</td>\n                <td>The access token (JWT) issued by the authorization server</td>\n            </tr>\n            <tr>\n                <td>token_type</td>\n                <td>describes the access token; value is always “Bearer”</td>\n            </tr>\n            <tr>\n                <td>expires_in</td>\n                <td>Lifetime in seconds of the access token, after which the token SHALL NOT be accepted by the resource server</td>\n            </tr>\n            <tr>\n                <td>scope</td>\n                <td>Scope of access authorized. Note that this can be different from the scopes requested by the app.</td>\n            </tr>\n            <tr>\n                <td>id_token</td>\n                <td>Authenticated user identity and user details, if requested</td>\n            </tr>\n            <tr>\n                <td>refresh_token</td>\n                <td>Token that can be used to obtain a new access token, using the same or a subset of the original authorization grants</td>\n            </tr>\n\n        </tbody>\n    </table>\n    <h3>\n        Token Refresh\n    </h3>\n    <p>\n        A Refresh Token is returned by the authorize endpoint when the offline_access scope is requested and obtained with the user’s authorization. To get an access token from a refresh token, you will need to form a new token request providing the refresh token in the refresh_token parameter and refresh_token as the value for the grant_type parameter. An app will also need to specify in the scope parameter which of the previously granted scopes your app would like included in the new access token.\n    </p>\n\n    <h3>PKCE Implementation</h3>\n    <p>\n        Token authentication using Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) is required by our authorization server for apps that cannot securely store a client secret. PKCE is a specification to the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow that requires your app to generate its own secret for each token request (called a “code verifier”) that can be verified by the authorization server (using a transformed value of the code verifier called a “code challenge”, which is passed in the authorize request along with the transformation method, or “code challenge method”). The code challenge and code challenge method must be provided in your app's authorize request and the code verifier sent in the token request.\n        For more information on PKCE, please visit the following <a href=\"https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7636\" target=\"_blank\">link</a>\n    </p>\n</body>\n</html>","numLines":228,"startLine":1,"totalLines":228}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01J83SkUXNSZsz7QMwLnDviP","type":"tool_result","content":"Capability\n\nDescription of Capability\n\nCosts or Fees\n\nUpdate and Setup\n\nThis includes the required program updates and configuration\nspecifically to use the Certified software to attest for the Quality\nPayment Program.\nAny special user training and setup specific to the practice performed\nby Systemedx beyond what is initially offered with the deployment of\nthe initial Update and Setup.\nAllows practice to include/exclude providers that wish to participate in\nthe Quality Payment Program. Providers without a license will not be\nable to have measure data reported for them.\n\nThis is a one-time fee.\n\nAdditional Training\nFee\nYearly Provider\nLicense\n\n\n\n\n\nElectronic\nPrescribing\n\nPatient Portal\nAccess\n\nThis is subject to an hourly fee dependent on the amount of time spent.\nThere is a yearly fee per provider to maintain and support the Certified product from\nyear to year.\n\n170.315(g)(1)/(g)(2) – Automated Measure Calculation\n170.315(c)(1) - Clinical Quality Measures – record and export\n170.315(c)(2) - Clinical Quality Measures – import and calculate\n170.315(c)(3) - Clinical Quality Measures - record\n\nThe ability to send an electronic prescription to the pharmacy.\nImpacted certification criteria may include:\n\n170.318(a)(1) -- CPOE - Medication\n\n170.315(a)(4) – Drug-drug, drug-allergy interactions\n\n(x) 170.315(a)(7) – Medication List\n\n(x) 170.315(a)(8) – Medication Allergy list\n\n170.315(a)(10) – Drug\n\nFormulary Checks\n\n170.315(a)(13) – Patient Specific Education\n\n170.315(b)(3) – Electronic Prescribing\n\n170.315(g)(2) /170.315(g)(2) – Automated Measure Calculation\nSecure Patient portal that enables patients to see records and communicate\nwith practice staff.\nImpacted certification criteria may include:\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\nTypes of costs or fees that a user may be required to pay to purchase, license, implement,\nmaintain, upgrade, use, or otherwise enable and support the use of the implementation or use\nof the capability -OR- in connection with the data generated in the course using the capability\n\n170.318(a)(1) -- CPOE - Medication\n170.315(a)(7) – Medication List\n170.315(a)(8) – Medication Allergy List\n170.315(a)(5) – Record Demographics\n(x) 170.315(a)(6) – Problem List\n(x) 170.315(a)(11) – Smoking Status\n170.315(a)(12) – Family Health History\n\nThere is a monthly fee from Systemedx per provider to be able to send electronic\nprescriptions to pharmacies.\nAn additional monthly charge from Systemedx may also be applied if a provider\nwishes to send controlled substances electronically to pharmacies. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01NGHR7CHZX1cRph2nzXPBTu","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_013e5H9xjBcL2FAGWUKNis76","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/systemedx-inc--systemedx-clinical-navigator/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# Systemedx Inc — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-15\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://www.systemedx.com/dataExport.html\n- CHPL IDs: 11536\n- Product: Systemedx Clinical Navigator v2024.12\n- Certification Date: 2024-11-26\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n1. **Initial probe**: `curl -sI -L \"https://www.systemedx.com/dataExport.html\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'` returned HTTP 200, Content-Type: text/html, Last-Modified: Thu, 05 May 2022 21:50:08 GMT. The page has not been modified since May 2022.\n\n2. **Page download**: `curl -sL \"https://www.systemedx.com/dataExport.html\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'` — 19,629 bytes of static HTML. No JavaScript rendering needed.\n\n3. **Content examination**: The page is a simple static HTML page with inline text describing the export module. There are **no download links** — no PDFs, ZIPs, CSVs, JSON schemas, or any other downloadable artifacts on the page. The entire documentation is ~150 words of inline text.\n\n4. **Link search**: `grep -oiE 'href=\"[^\"]*\\.(pdf|zip|xlsx|csv|json)\"' page.html` returned nothing. No downloadable files linked from this page.\n\n5. **MIPS/Mandatory Disclosures page** (`mipssolutions.html`): Found three links:\n   - \"Other Mandatory Disclosures\" → `images/Mandatory Disclosures 2022.pdf` (downloaded)\n   - \"Real World Test Plans\" → `images/RWT Website.zip` (not relevant to EHI export)\n   - \"DataExport\" → `dataExport.html` (the same page already examined)\n\n6. **Mandatory Disclosures PDF**: Downloaded and examined. 2-page cost transparency document listing fees for various capabilities (e-prescribing, patient portal, lab interfaces, API access at $10,000/year/app). Does not mention the (b)(10) data export module or any associated costs.\n\n7. **FHIR API documentation** (separate system): Checked `API/Header.html` which links to:\n   - APIIntro.html — introduction page, links to endpoint.json\n   - AuthorizationTechnical.html — OAuth 2.0 authorization docs\n   - AppRegistration.html — app registration process\n   - SupportedResources.html — FHIR resource listing (standard US Core IG 4.0.0 / USCDI v1)\n   - These are (g)(10) FHIR API documentation, not (b)(10) export documentation\n\n8. **SupportedResources.html** lists standard USCDI v1 resources: AllergyIntolerance, CarePlan, CareTeam, Condition, Device, DiagnosticReport, DocumentReference, Encounter, Goal, Immunization, Medication, MedicationRequest, MedicationDispense, Observation, Patient, Coverage, Procedure, ServiceRequest, Specimen, Provenance, SmokingStatus, VitalSigns, Location, Organization, Practitioner, BulkExport, Binary. All standard US Core — no custom resources or vendor-specific extensions.\n\n9. **Alternative paths probed**: Checked `ehi.html`, `b10.html`, `bulk.html`, `export.html`, `data-dictionary.html`, `schema.html`, `datadictionary.html` — all returned 404.\n\n10. **Wayback Machine**: CDX API shows 3 snapshots (2022-05-29, 2024-10-15, 2025-06-24), all returning the same content. The page has been unchanged since creation.\n\n11. **Screenshot**: Captured full-page screenshot of dataExport.html.\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThe EHI export documentation consists of a single static HTML page with approximately 150 words of inline text. There are no downloadable files, no data dictionary, no schema, and no field-level documentation.\n\n### The Export Module\n\nThe export is accessed via a job stream called \"CDAEXPORT\" which appears in the application as \"Data Export.\" It has three modes:\n\n1. **All Patients** — exports all patients with configurable date range, output directory, and options for chart documents and human-readable CDA copy\n2. **Select Patients** — same options but allows selecting a subset of patients manually or by appointment date range\n3. **Single Patient** — same options but limited to one patient\n\n### Export Format\n\nThe export produces:\n- **CDA XML files** — patient demographics and \"distinct chart data\" (medications, problems, etc.)\n- **CDA.html files** — human-readable HTML versions of the CDA documents\n- **PDF documents** — patient chart documents, organized in a \"Documents\" folder with subfolders by document type\n\nFiles are organized into patient folders named: `LastName_FirstName_DOB_PatientID`\n\n### What's NOT Documented\n\nThe documentation does not specify:\n- Which CDA template or standard is used (C-CDA R2.1? Custom CDA? What sections?)\n- What \"distinct chart data\" means — which data elements beyond \"medications, problems, etc.\"\n- What document types exist in the Documents folder\n- What date ranges mean — encounter dates? modified dates?\n- File encoding, character sets, or XML schemas\n- How relationships between records are preserved\n- Whether billing, surgical pathway, or practice management data is included\n- Sample files or examples\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nBased on the product research, Systemedx Clinical Navigator stores data across these domains:\n\n| Domain | Covered by Export? | Evidence |\n|--------|-------------------|----------|\n| Patient demographics | Likely partial | Mentioned in CDA export (\"patient demographics\") |\n| Clinical encounters/visit notes | Unknown | Not mentioned; may be in CDA or PDF documents |\n| Medications | Likely partial | Explicitly mentioned (\"medications\") |\n| Problems/diagnoses | Likely partial | Explicitly mentioned (\"problems\") |\n| Lab results | Unknown | Not mentioned |\n| Allergies | Unknown | Not mentioned (but standard CDA section) |\n| Vital signs | Unknown | Not mentioned |\n| Immunizations | Unknown | Not mentioned |\n| Orders (lab, imaging) | Unknown | Not mentioned |\n| Billing/claims data (CPT, ICD, claims, remittances) | **Likely absent** | No mention of billing data; CDA format does not naturally carry billing information |\n| Scheduling/appointments | N/A | Operational data, not EHI |\n| Surgical pathway data (case tracking, task lists) | **Likely absent** | No mention; this is a key product differentiator with no apparent export coverage |\n| Patient portal messages | Unknown | Not mentioned |\n| Quality measures data | Unknown | Not mentioned |\n| Documents/images | Yes | Explicitly included as PDF exports |\n| E-prescribing/PDMP data | Unknown | Not mentioned |\n| Insurance/enrollment data | Unknown | Not mentioned |\n\nThe documentation is so sparse that most domains fall into \"unknown.\" The export appears to be CDA-based, which inherently limits it to the CDA document model — primarily clinical summaries. The phrase \"distinct chart data\" is undefined and could mean anything from a full C-CDA with all sections to a minimal patient summary.\n\n**Critical gap**: There is no mention of billing, claims, or financial data. For a product that includes full practice management with AI-assisted coding, claims submission, and surgical billing recovery, the absence of billing data from the export is a significant concern. Billing records are squarely within the designated record set.\n\n**Critical gap**: The surgical pathways module — a differentiating feature that tracks surgical cases, billing recovery, and pre/post-op workflows — has no apparent representation in the export.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe export uses CDA XML, which is a recognized clinical document standard. However:\n\n- The specific CDA template/profile is not documented. If it's C-CDA R2.1, the data would include standard sections (allergies, medications, problems, procedures, results, vital signs, immunizations, etc.) — but this is not confirmed.\n- CDA is a document format designed for clinical summaries, not comprehensive data export. It does not naturally accommodate billing data, surgical pathway tracking, practice management data, or many types of specialty-specific clinical data.\n- PDF export of chart documents is a reasonable supplement for unstructured content.\n- The folder structure (`LastName_FirstName_DOB_PatientID`) is clear for organizing per-patient exports.\n\nA third party receiving this export would have CDA XML documents (with unknown sections/completeness), human-readable HTML copies, and PDF chart documents. Without knowing the CDA template, it's impossible to assess whether the XML would enable meaningful data import into another system.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThe documentation quality is **very poor**:\n\n- **No data dictionary**: There is no field-level documentation whatsoever\n- **No schema**: No XSD, JSON Schema, or any machine-readable specification\n- **No examples**: No sample CDA files, no sample export structure\n- **No section inventory**: The CDA sections included are not listed\n- **No value sets**: No coded terminology documentation\n- **~150 words total**: The entire documentation is shorter than most email signatures\n- **Unchanged since 2022**: The Last-Modified header shows May 2022, predating the current certification (November 2024). The documentation was not updated for the certification cycle.\n- **No developer guidance**: A developer could not implement an import of this data based on this documentation alone. They would need to obtain a sample export and reverse-engineer it.\n\nThis documentation reads as a compliance checkbox — the absolute minimum needed to have a URL to register with CHPL. It describes how to trigger the export but not what the export contains.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity**: The documentation provides zero field-level detail. It mentions \"medications, problems, etc.\" as examples of chart data but does not enumerate sections, fields, data types, or cardinality.\n- **Relationships**: No documentation of how records relate to each other.\n- **Value sets**: No documentation of coded values.\n- **Versioning**: No version history. Page unchanged since May 2022.\n\n### (b)(10) vs (g)(10) Assessment\n\nSystemedx has a clear separation between the (b)(10) and (g)(10) mechanisms:\n- **(g)(10)**: FHIR R4 API with US Core IG 4.0.0 / USCDI v1 resources, OAuth 2.0 authorization, documented across multiple pages under `/API/`\n- **(b)(10)**: CDA-based \"CDAEXPORT\" module with PDF document export, documented on the single `dataExport.html` page\n\nThe (b)(10) export is not repackaged FHIR — it's a genuinely separate CDA-based export mechanism. However, the CDA format may limit what data can be exported, and the documentation is far too sparse to determine whether the export actually covers \"all electronic health information\" as required.\n\nThe (g)(10) FHIR API covers standard USCDI clinical data. The (b)(10) export should cover everything beyond USCDI — billing, surgical pathways, practice management data — but there's no evidence it does.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://www.systemedx.com/dataExport.html\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- No sitemap.xml or robots.txt on the domain (both 404)\n- No downloadable artifacts linked from the export page\n- Wayback Machine confirmed page has been unchanged since May 2022\n- FHIR API documentation exists separately under `/API/` but is (g)(10), not (b)(10)\n- Probed multiple alternative paths (ehi.html, b10.html, bulk.html, export.html, data-dictionary.html, schema.html, datadictionary.html) — all 404\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":346,"cache_read_input_tokens":74380,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":346},"output_tokens":4,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"98e6820a-4840-46d0-8f7d-956071973dc2","uuid":"2450681f-8caa-487b-be81-d85cda6b95c8"}

Billing records are squarely within the designated record set.\n\n**Critical gap**: The surgical pathways module — a differentiating feature that tracks surgical cases, billing recovery, and pre/post-op workflows — has no apparent representation in the export.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe export uses CDA XML, which is a recognized clinical document standard. However:\n\n- The specific CDA template/profile is not documented. If it's C-CDA R2.1, the data would include standard sections (allergies, medications, problems, procedures, results, vital signs, immunizations, etc.) — but this is not confirmed.\n- CDA is a document format designed for clinical summaries, not comprehensive data export. It does not naturally accommodate billing data, surgical pathway tracking, practice management data, or many types of specialty-specific clinical data.\n- PDF export of chart documents is a reasonable supplement for unstructured content.\n- The folder structure (`LastName_FirstName_DOB_PatientID`) is clear for organizing per-patient exports.\n\nA third party receiving this export would have CDA XML documents (with unknown sections/completeness), human-readable HTML copies, and PDF chart documents. Without knowing the CDA template, it's impossible to assess whether the XML would enable meaningful data import into another system.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThe documentation quality is **very poor**:\n\n- **No data dictionary**: There is no field-level documentation whatsoever\n- **No schema**: No XSD, JSON Schema, or any machine-readable specification\n- **No examples**: No sample CDA files, no sample export structure\n- **No section inventory**: The CDA sections included are not listed\n- **No value sets**: No coded terminology documentation\n- **~150 words total**: The entire documentation is shorter than most email signatures\n- **Unchanged since 2022**: The Last-Modified header shows May 2022, predating the current certification (November 2024). The documentation was not updated for the certification cycle.\n- **No developer guidance**: A developer could not implement an import of this data based on this documentation alone. They would need to obtain a sample export and reverse-engineer it.\n\nThis documentation reads as a compliance checkbox — the absolute minimum needed to have a URL to register with CHPL. It describes how to trigger the export but not what the export contains.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity**: The documentation provides zero field-level detail. It mentions \"medications, problems, etc.\" as examples of chart data but does not enumerate sections, fields, data types, or cardinality.\n- **Relationships**: No documentation of how records relate to each other.\n- **Value sets**: No documentation of coded values.\n- **Versioning**: No version history. Page unchanged since May 2022.\n\n### (b)(10) vs (g)(10) Assessment\n\nSystemedx has a clear separation between the (b)(10) and (g)(10) mechanisms:\n- **(g)(10)**: FHIR R4 API with US Core IG 4.0.0 / USCDI v1 resources, OAuth 2.0 authorization, documented across multiple pages under `/API/`\n- **(b)(10)**: CDA-based \"CDAEXPORT\" module with PDF document export, documented on the single `dataExport.html` page\n\nThe (b)(10) export is not repackaged FHIR — it's a genuinely separate CDA-based export mechanism. However, the CDA format may limit what data can be exported, and the documentation is far too sparse to determine whether the export actually covers \"all electronic health information\" as required.\n\nThe (g)(10) FHIR API covers standard USCDI clinical data. The (b)(10) export should cover everything beyond USCDI — billing, surgical pathways, practice management data — but there's no evidence it does.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://www.systemedx.com/dataExport.html\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- No sitemap.xml or robots.txt on the domain (both 404)\n- No downloadable artifacts linked from the export page\n- Wayback Machine confirmed page has been unchanged since May 2022\n- FHIR API documentation exists separately under `/API/` but is (g)(10), not (b)(10)\n- Probed multiple alternative paths (ehi.html, b10.html, bulk.html, export.html, data-dictionary.html, schema.html, datadictionary.html) — all 404\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null}}
